newsitem.title: USA: U.S. joyrider's tour forces jet to abort landing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. joyrider's tour forces jet to abort landing.

text.p: An airborne joy-rider stole a light plane and took an unauthorised tour of north Texas airfields, forcing a passenger jet to abort its landing at Dallas-Fort Worth airport, officials said on Saturday.

The unknown pilot apparently stole the single-engine Cessna 172 plane and buzzed the Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport at low altitude on Friday afternoon, messing up the landing approach of an American Airlines flight from Frankfurt, Germany with 204 passengers and 10 crew on board.
The American Airlines plane had to go around, Roland Herwig, a local spokesman for the Federal Aviation Administration, said Saturday.
The pilot also flew through the traffic patterns at nearby Fort Worth Alliance airport and at Bell Helicopter's airstrip near Fort Worth on the half-hour tour.
The plane's owner, John Hooker, a mechanic at Sherman Municipal Airport, said he was at lunch when his plane was performing its escapades and that it was parked in a different spot when he returned.
He said several people have keys to the plane and he was not sure who had taken it. "When I find him, I'm going to start by strangling him to get his attention," Hooker told The Dallas Morning News.
Herwig said federal officials were trying to track down the joyrider, and might suspend his license and fine him. Criminal charges could also be filed by local police.

We take this very seriously," Herwig said, adding that such cases were unusual but not unheard of. "It's often not a malicious act on the part of anybody. Airspaces are complex and people sometimes violate them without prior knowledge, but they're still responsible for it".
